gold_violations.description: adc_sample_q is a multi-bit value produced in adc_clk and sampled directly in dsp_clk without a bundled-data handshake or hold guarantee.

Per-bit or raw sampling of sensor_status_i is consumed as one cfg-domain status word; bit skew can create values that never existed in the sensor domain.
sensor_event_pulse_i is a one-cycle sensor_clk pulse sampled directly by cfg_clk, so events can be missed when cfg_clk is slower or phase shifted.
sensor_event_toggle_i is compared through one history flop, allowing metastability or double-counting because the current async value reconverges with the sampled value.
sensor_valid_i controls capture of sensor_payload_i without a source hold/acknowledge contract for the payload bundle.
Low and high timestamp halves are captured in different cfg_clk cycles, allowing impossible mixed-cycle timestamps.
The parity reduction of sensor_crc_i can glitch and enable cfg-domain state updates using a metastable or incoherent CRC value.
sensor_rst_n_i is consumed as a synchronous cfg-domain event, so reset deassertion can metastably alter cfg_status_word_o.
sensor_mode_i bits are synchronized independently and then decoded as cfg_mode_shadow_o; skew can create illegal transient modes.
sensor_threshold_shadow_i is a sensor-domain mirror of cfg_threshold_o copied back into cfg_clk, creating a stale or incoherent feedback path.
gray_count_o appears Gray encoded, but the producer can increment by more than one under test_mode, invalidating one-bit-change CDC assumptions.
debug_trigger_i crosses from debug_clk to cfg_clk and is edge-detected using the raw async value against one sampled copy.
scan_enable_i selects scan_clk versus cfg_clk for state normally owned by cfg logic without a safe integrated clock mux or mode constraint.
axi_desc_valid_o is driven by cmd_sync_q, a two-flop level synchronization of cfg_cmd_pulse_i that can miss narrow pulses or stretch them into multiple AXI commands.
axi_descriptor_o captures cfg_descriptor_i based on cmd_sync_q without ensuring cfg_descriptor_i is stable across the AXI capture window.
cfg_addr_i and cfg_wdata_i are sampled in axi_clk when cmd_sync_q is high, but the sideband values are not acknowledged or held atomically.
irq_o combines a synchronized cfg_irq_enable_i with raw dsp_irq_req_i in axi_clk, creating a multi-source reconvergent CDC path.
cfg_reset_req_i gates AXI status state directly from cfg_clk with no synchronizer or handshake.
cfg_rst_n_i is consumed inside axi_clk logic, so the deasserting reset edge is an uncontrolled CDC event.
mem_done_toggle_i is XORed against a single AXI sample, allowing metastability or double pulses in axi_status_word_o.
